consequences: Tap latencies are ~2.2x the stock environment but the per-environment 80 ms fused_neural budget still passes (p95 74.67 ms).

The CTC beam search cannot complete within its 1500 ms standalone budget under interpretation; rows bail at the deadline and the bail path returns partial or empty candidate sets, so swipe quality metrics on this environment are latency-censored, not model-quality measurements (ctc top-1 0.0, fused_swipe top-1 0.07, while pure-Java geometric still completes some rows at top-1 0.36).
One-time fixture costs inflate: swipeLexicon build 130,298 ms vs 22,751 ms on stock.
evidence: logcat ArtService: compiler filter adjusted from 'speed' to 'verify' because the package is debuggable
pm art dump org.libreboard.keyboard.debug -> [status=run-from-apk] before forced compile, [status=verify] after; 'speed' is unreachable for debuggable builds
/proc/<pid>/task/*/comm shows no 'Jit thread' for the instrumentation process or for any other app on the device
the same APK on the stock Pixel 7 Pro environment reaches fused p50 15.7 ms taps and 68 ms CTC decodes; this environment records 37.1 ms and deadline-pinned >=1500 ms
followUps: A non-debuggable testOnly measurement build (corpora via instrumentation args instead of run-as) would restore representative latency on this environment for a future pin.
The deadline bail returning garbage candidates is a product defect worth fixing independently: bailing should fall back to the geometric candidate set.
environmentCondition.headline: The pinned debug APK runs fully interpreted on this environment: GrapheneOS disables the JIT system-wide (dalvik.vm.usejit=false; stock Android ships true), and AOSP ArtService policy caps debuggable packages to verify-only AOT ('Adjusting the compiler filter ... from speed to verify because the package is debuggable'). No app process on the device, including system release apps, has a JIT thread. Release (non-debuggable) LibreBoard builds receive normal AOT dexopt and are unaffected, so this condition bounds the debug measurement harness, not the product.

findings: The tap commit decision survives full interpretation: fused beats classic by +31.1% relative error reduction (stock environment: +33.6%; gate >= +20%), with zero false corrections, and the fused_neural p95 74.67 ms stays inside the 80 ms budget despite running interpreted.

GrapheneOS's system-wide JIT disable is invisible to release apps (AOT dexopt) but leaves debuggable instrumentation builds fully interpreted; all per-row latency on this environment measures the interpreter, roughly 2.2x compiled speed on tap paths and unbounded on the CTC beam loop.

Swipe metrics on this environment are deadline-censored and must not be read as model quality: CTC cannot finish 1500 ms of interpreted beam search, and the bail path returns partial or empty candidates (ctc top-1 0.0). This was also true of the superseded September diagnostics on this same phone (fused p50 26.8 ms, neural overhead +12.4 ms), which retroactively explains their signature.
The swipe lexicon build costs 130 s one-time under interpretation (stock: 22.7 s); it is excluded from latencyMs but dominates cold-start cost in this condition.
limitations: Second of three environments; pooled matrix gates cannot be evaluated until the low-RAM leg lands on shard 2/3.
Per-row latency measures the debug harness under GrapheneOS's no-JIT configuration; it is an upper bound, not representative of AOT-compiled release builds.
Swipe rows are exactly at the evaluator's per-environment 100-sample floor.
The single-environment diagnostic script mirrors evaluate_engine.py semantics but is not the release evaluator; its output is not release evidence.

measurement.evaluatorPrecheck: Pooled with the stock leg (30,482 rows), every row parses the schema-4 contract and the evaluator rejects the metadata only with 'metadata requires exactly the three reference environments' (low_ram_emulator still missing), as designed.

measurement.swipeRowCountNote: Planned as the first 300 rows of swipe shard 1/3; the harness applies its own ordinal shard filter to the pushed corpus, so the pre-sharded file was filtered again and the run measured the 100 rows whose in-file ordinal is 1 mod 3. Exactly meets the evaluator's 100-sample per-environment swipe minimum; pooled swipe minimums are already satisfied by the stock leg. Rows remain disjoint from shards 0 and 2.

scope: GrapheneOS physical hardware environment leg of the Phase 0 device matrix, collected under the artifact pin with the schema-4 harness. Measured with the pinned debug APK under GrapheneOS's system-wide JIT-disabled configuration, which leaves debuggable builds fully interpreted; see environmentCondition. Qualifying pooled evaluation remains blocked until the low-RAM leg takes shard 2/3; until then these are the grapheneos-environment numbers a pooled evaluation will use.
